newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bundesbank urged to breathe life into Bubill mkt.
newsitem.headline: Bundesbank urged to breathe life into Bubill mkt.

text.p: German money dealers on Tuesday urged the Bundesbank to start conducting market-smoothing transactions to help cultivate a secondary market for six-month Treasury discount paper, or Bubills.

With outstanding debt of just 20 billion marks the Bubills lack liquidity and there is virtually no secondary market for the paper, Detlef Bindert, board member of the Association of German Money Market Traders (VDG), said.

"Large players like some central banks have already quit the market," Bindert told a news conference given by the Association. Given the lack of liquidity, dealers were unable to buy or sell Bubills whenever they wanted to.

Bindert, a money market trader at Deutsche Bank AG, said Bubills currently traded at a large spread of 15 basis points over LIBID, the London Interbank Bid Rate, the rate at which banks take deposits from each other.
The Bundesbank does not conduct market-smoothing deals for Bubills but it does do so for one and two-year German government paper.
The bank only last year gave its grudging approval to the issue of government debt with a maturity of less than one year.

It had resisted the move for years, arguing that short-term debt issuance could hamper its monetary policy by creating a potential for conflict with the government, whose borrowing costs would be directly affected by interest rate changes.

The Bundesbank finally agreed to approve short-term debt for the sake of the German debt market. The move has plugged a gaping hole in the German yield curve and could help Germany compete with rival financial centres where short-term government debt issuance is common practice.
But the bank set a limit of 20 billion marks on the outstanding volume of such paper, whereas money traders regard a volume of 50 billion marks as essential to develop a functioning secondary market.
The Bundesbank said on Tuesday it will set an auction for about nine billion marks of Bubills on April 15.
